says: On her laptop Alice submits one record of each contract through its owner in submit mode: her device key binding (C01 principal_binding), her private notes source's home (C01 source_home), its first revision on the head the registration made (C01 source_manifest), and, after founding a team on the same device key, its binding to a GitHub repository (C09 carrier_binding); every request is itself a sealed C03 operation_request. Each owner answers with the record it stored: the submitted fields exactly as submitted, plus only the fields the runtime owns — the binding id and time, the registration time, the revision's production time, the carrier binding id and bound time; each commit also writes its C03 receipt. The revision is then read back twice by a reference to its member, and each read returns the same stored revision and home under the same digests; the key binding is queried twice by request id, and each query returns the same original result and receipt; the carrier binding's own request is submitted again twice, and each answer returns the same stored binding and digest, unchanged. What must not happen: a stored record whose submitted fields changed, a runtime-owned field taken from the submission, or a second read returning other bytes or another digest.
